paper_a.title: Entropy Compression Method and Legitimate Colorings in Projective Planes

paper_b.title: Application of entropy compression in pattern avoidance

metadata.description: Both papers apply the Esperet-Parreau entropy compression method (a refinement of Moser-Tardos) to two different combinatorial-existence problems: paper A (Bissacot-Doin) constructs legitimate d-colorings of finite projective planes by avoiding 'dangerous pairs' of lines, while paper B (Ochem-Pinlou) constructs infinite words over Sigma avoiding all instances of a pattern p. The shared backbone is identical: a randomized iterative algorithm whose execution is recorded into a compact 'register/record' object such that the input is recoverable from the (record, current state) pair, hence (by an entropy / counting argument tracing back to Moser-Tardos) the algorithm must terminate. Paper A explicitly proves a generalized Esperet-Parreau bound (Theorem 1) as a self-contained tool; paper B cites the same Esperet-Parreau result for partial-Dyck-word asymptotics. The two papers attack disjoint combinatorial objects (projective-plane line types vs words over a finite alphabet), so the relationship is same-method (SM) rather than EXT/CF/PR.

matches.explanation: Both algorithms instantiate the Esperet-Parreau / Moser-Tardos entropy-compression template. AP418.1 (modified Moser-Tardos) iteratively assigns sampled values to the smallest-index uncolored variable and, on creating a bad setting, uncolors the involved variables and records (alpha,beta,gamma) in register R; AP411.1 (AvoidPattern) iteratively appends a binary input bit to a word w and, on creating an occurrence of pattern p, erases the suffix of length l and records this in R=(D,L,X). Different state spaces (variable family vs binary word) and different 'bad configurations' (LLL bad events vs pattern occurrences), but identical control flow: append/sample, detect bad event, retract, log into record, repeat.

Both define the bookkeeping object that makes the entropy-compression argument work. DP418.4's register vector R stores at each step a triple (alpha=l_y, beta in [d_l_y], gamma in [m_y]) recording the size, position and value-label of the bad event triggered. DP411.6's record R=(D,L,X) is a triplet where D is a binary word marking append-vs-erase steps, L stores (k-1)-sets of integers describing the erased occurrence's structure, and X stores the variable-content bits. Same conceptual role (a per-step trace whose total entropy can be bounded) with different decompositions tailored to each object.

Both are the central injectivity / reconstruction lemma that drives the entropy-compression contradiction. LP418.2 says ((R_j)_{j<=i}, phi_i) suffices to deduce all colors used through step i; LP411.2 (Lemma 4) says (R_i, w_i) permits recovery of the input prefix V_i. These are the same statement transposed to two domains: 'the (record, current state) pair is an injective encoding of the algorithm's history.' Both proofs (PP418.1 and PP411.3) proceed by induction on i with a case split on whether the latest record entry indicates a bad event or not.

LP418.1 is an auxiliary lemma stating that the set X_i of uncolored variables after step i is a function of (R_j)_{j<=i} alone. Paper B's algorithm has no analogous 'uncolored set' notion (it works with a single growing/shrinking word w), and Lemma 4 of paper B folds the corresponding bookkeeping directly into the recovery of V_i from (R_i,w_i). Paper-specific scaffolding.

Both proofs establish the injectivity / reconstruction lemma by induction on the step counter i, splitting cases on what the most recent register/record entry records. PP418.1 splits on R_i empty vs R_i=(alpha,beta,gamma); PP411.3 splits on D ending in 0 (no occurrence) vs D ending in 01^l (occurrence of length l erased). Same proof skeleton, different per-step state transitions.

Composite L2 cluster: the per-step decomposition of the injectivity-by-induction proof. PSP418.1 ~ PSP411.8 (base case), PSP418.3 ~ PSP411.9 (no-bad-event case where the last colored variable / appended letter is read off directly), PSP418.4 ~ PSP411.10 (bad-event/occurrence case where the record's structured entry reverse-engineers the previous state). PSP418.2 has no direct analogue because paper B does not separate out a 'use of LP418.1 to identify which variable was colored' step.

Paper A's Theorem 1 (a self-contained variant of Esperet-Parreau) yields the existence of a coloring avoiding all bad settings using ceil(gamma * sup_i (d_l_i m_i)^{1/l_i}) colors, with phi_E(x)=1+sum_{i in E} x^i and tau satisfying phi_E(tau) - tau phi_E'(tau) = 0. Paper B's Lemma 6 (Esperet-Parreau Dyck-word asymptotics) takes phi_d(x) = 1 + sum_{i>=d} x^i = 1 + x^d/(1-x) and uses the same critical-equation phi_d(tau) - tau phi_d'(tau) = 0 to bound the partial-Dyck count C_{t,d} <= c_d gamma_d^t t^{-3/2}. Both isolate the same singularity-analysis kernel of the entropy-compression bound; paper A names it as a theorem while paper B cites it as a lemma from Esperet-Parreau.

Both papers cite the same external Esperet-Parreau (2012/2013) entropy-compression result. TP418.2 names the original Esperet-Parreau theorem; LP411.3 (partial-Dyck reduction C_{t,r,d} <= C_{t+d-1,d}) and LP411.4 (Dyck asymptotics) are the Esperet-Parreau lemmas paper B reuses. External-vs-external citation match: same underlying result invoked as prior art on both sides.

DP418.3 is the cited Moser-Tardos / Kolipaka-Szegedy 'variable version of the Lovasz Local Lemma' setup (independent discrete random variables, bad events depending on subsets). Paper B does not formalize an LLL setting at all -- it works directly with words and pattern occurrences -- so this external scaffolding has no B-side counterpart. External-origin, but kept as 'none' to record the asymmetric LLL framing.

ProbP418.2 (variable-version forbidden-configuration coloring) asks for a vertex coloring of V avoiding all bad settings (Z,c). Paper B's DP411.2 defines the avoidability index lambda(p) as the smallest alphabet size admitting an infinite p-avoiding word; the underlying problem (find a coloring/labelling avoiding a specified class of forbidden configurations using the fewest symbols) is the same. Cross-type match (problem vs definition) justified because DP411.2 is functionally paper B's 'main problem statement'.

Both encode the 'forbidden configuration' substrate used by the entropy-compression algorithm. DP418.1/DP418.2 define a bad setting (Z,c) with vertex subset Z and forbidden coloring c, plus the indexing data (k_i, m_i, l_i, d_l) used in the bound. DP411.3 defines an occurrence of pattern p as an assignment of non-empty words to each variable that produces a specific factor in w. Different vocabularies (graph-vertex coloring vs word factor) but the same role: 'a witness that the current partial configuration is forbidden.'

DP418.7 (dangerous pair: two distinct lines whose type vectors differ by at most 22 ln n in l_1 distance) is the projective-plane-specific definition of the bad event the algorithm tries to avoid. Paper B has no notion of line types, so this is paper-A-specific.

DP418.8 (optimal block size m_bar = argmin (m/(m-1))(m! a b (m-1))^{1/m}) is the projective-plane-tuned scalar parameter chosen to minimize Theorem 1's bound. Paper B carries an analogous optimization implicitly inside Lemma 6 (choice of d via phi_d(tau)-tau phi_d'(tau)=0) but does not isolate a 'block size' quantity, and any cross-paper match here would be an artefact of the shared Esperet-Parreau lemma rather than a real correspondence. Listed as paper-A-specific to keep the alignment honest.

Fact 1 (existence of S with (1/2) ln n <= |line cap S| <= 11 ln n via probabilistic method + McDiarmid bounded-differences) is a projective-plane-specific probabilistic-method ingredient with no analogue in paper B's word-avoidance argument.
Cardinality bound on the hitting set S: paper-A-specific corollary feeding into the projective-plane construction; no counterpart in pattern-avoidance machinery.

Fact 2 (existence of a partial coloring of P_n - S with bounded-incidence dangerous pairs) is the projective-plane-specific 'preprocessing' that gets fed into the entropy-compression call (TP418.1). No analogue in paper B, which feeds the algorithm an arbitrary input vector V.

Both are the paper's main quantitative output obtained by feeding the entropy-compression machinery with the right preprocessing. PrP418.3 produces a legitimate d-coloring of P_n with max(d(n,a,b), ceil min_m (m/(m-1))(m! a b (m-1))^{1/m}) colors. TP411.2 produces avoidability bounds lambda(p) <= 3 (for |p| >= 2^k) and lambda(p) = 2 (for |p| >= 3*2^{k-1}). Same role (final existence theorem proved via entropy compression), distinct combinatorial objects, hence analogous rather than exact.

Both proofs combine the paper's preprocessing with the entropy-compression bound to yield the main result. PP418.5 fixes the partial coloring from Fact 2, computes tau and phi_E'(tau) for E={m_bar}, and applies Theorem 1. PP411.4 (proof of Theorem 2.b) sets up a contradiction, runs AvoidPattern on a binary input, decomposes |R| = |D|*|L|*|X| and uses Lemmas 5, 6 to conclude |R| = o(2^t), contradicting |V| = 2^t. The two proofs play the same role (final assembly) but use different argument structures (constructive existence in A vs proof-by-contradiction in B).

Proofs of the projective-plane preprocessing facts (PP418.2 of Corollary on |S|; PP418.3 of Fact 1 via McDiarmid; PP418.4 of Fact 2 via Alon-Furedi probabilistic method). All paper-A-specific, with no pattern-avoidance counterpart.

Numerical bounds K, P_a, P_b for paper A's probabilistic Fact-2 argument; specific to projective planes / dangerous pairs. Paper B has its own numerical bounds (EP411.3 on gamma_d, EP411.4 final contradiction inequality) that play structurally similar roles inside the entropy-compression contradiction, but at the level of node-by-node correspondence the actual quantities are paper-specific. Listed under A as 'none' to avoid forcing spurious matches.
DP411.1 (pattern p over a variable alphabet Delta and instance via non-erasing morphism) is paper-B-specific terminology with no paper-A analogue.

Doubled and balanced patterns are pattern-avoidance-specific structural notions (every variable appears >= 2 times, with the balanced-prefix/suffix condition). Paper A has no analogous structural classification of bad settings.

DP411.7 (partial Dyck word, descent of length d) and DP411.8 (generating series phi_d(x) = 1 + x^d/(1-x)) are the singularity-analysis ingredients used to bound |D|. Paper A's Theorem 1 uses a different but conceptually parallel phi_E(x) = 1 + sum_{i in E} x^i (matched at TP418.1 <-> LP411.4 above). Listing the underlying definitions as paper-B-specific avoids a chain of speculative cross-matches; the conceptual link is captured by the TP418.1 <-> LP411.4 entry.
h_k(l), g_k(l) are pattern-avoidance-specific counting functions for length-l factors; no paper-A counterpart.

Claim 1 (reduction from arbitrary patterns of length >= f * 2^{k-1} to balanced patterns) is paper-B-specific preprocessing for the avoidability theorem. Conceptually parallel to paper A's Facts 1-2 preprocessing (reduce the projective-plane problem to a manageable partial coloring), but the specific reduction technique has no node-level analogue.

Theorem 2.(a) packaged as a corollary -- paper-B-specific instance of the main result; covered structurally by the PrP418.3 <-> TP411.2 match above, listed here as 'none' only because CP411.1 is a separate node.
Proofs of Claim 1 and Theorem 2.(a) -- paper-B-specific reductions (induction on variable count, collapse high-multiplicity variables, invoke Bell-Goh). No paper-A analogue.

EP411.1 polynomial form of phi_d - x phi_d' = 0, EP411.2 OGF for length-tuples, EP411.4 final contradiction inequality 2^t <= 2^n |R| = o(2^t). All paper-B-specific quantitative ingredients of the contradiction-by-counting argument; no node-level paper-A counterpart (paper A's bound is constructive, not a contradiction).
